source_reachability:
I re-fetched every URL myself on 2026-09-16 with `curl -sS -A "Mokaair-editorial" -L` and checked the body, not just the status.

SOURCES AS RECORDED (all 4 genuinely reachable, real article bodies, no redirects, no challenge/denied pages):
1. https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-m6-and-m5-ultra-for-a-big-leap-in-performance-and-ai-compute/ — HTTP 200, 201,731 B, 0 redirects, body is the real press release ("PRESS RELEASE", "August 25, 2026", full text + footnotes + press contacts).
2. https://www.apple.com/tw/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-m6-and-m5-ultra-for-a-big-leap-in-performance-and-ai-compute/ — HTTP 200, 195,266 B, lang="zh-TW", genuine Traditional-Chinese translation ("新聞發佈 / 2026 年 8 月 25 日").
3. https://www.apple.com/tw/newsroom/2026/08/apple-unveils-a-more-powerful-mac-mini-featuring-the-all-new-m6-and-m5-pro/ — HTTP 200, 225,209 B, lang="zh-TW", real body incl. NT$ pricing block.
4. https://www.apple.com/tw/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-new-mac-studio-with-m5-max-and-m5-ultra/ — HTTP 200, 212,252 B, lang="zh-TW", real body incl. NT$ pricing block.

NOT IN sources BUT CITED INSIDE verified_facts (32 of 60 facts point at these two URLs, which the record itself admits are not in `sources`):
5. https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-unveils-a-more-powerful-mac-mini-featuring-the-all-new-m6-and-m5-pro/ — HTTP 200, 235,077 B.
6. https://www.apple.com/newsroom/2026/08/apple-introduces-new-mac-studio-with-m5-max-and-m5-ultra/ — HTTP 200, 231,931 B.

CORROBORATION CHANNELS I CHECKED MYSELF:
- https://www.apple.com/newsroom/rss-feed.rss — HTTP 200, 18,825 B, Atom, 20 <entry>, newest 2026-09-16, OLDEST 2026-08-11. It contains all three 2026-08-25 items with <updated> 2026-08-25, independently corroborating the event date and the three URLs.
- https://www.apple.com/newsroom/archive/ — HTTP 200, 322,881 B; contains 10 article links (all 2026-09), i.e. it is NOT empty to curl.

All six article URLs are first-party apple.com. No news outlet, aggregator, law-firm blog or search snippet appears anywhere in `sources` or in any fact's `url`. No URL, document number or identifier in the record looks guessed: the /tw/ paths mirror the US paths and I confirmed each returns 200 with real translated content; the recorded source `title` values match each page's own <title>/og:title byte-for-byte.

LIVE-DOCUMENT WARNING (researcher missed this): every one of the six pages carries JSON-LD "datePublished": "2026-08-25Z" AND "dateModified": "2026-08-27T13:59-14:09Z". These are revised pages, so the record should state which version was read (fetched 2026-09-16, dateModified 2026-08-27).

refuted.fact: event_date_basis: 「這些頁面沒有暴露 JSON-LD 的 datePublished／dateModified，Apple 自己顯示的日期是唯一官方日期訊號」
refuted.why: REFUTED by direct inspection. All six pages embed application/ld+json with "datePublished": "2026-08-25Z" and "dateModified": "2026-08-27T13:59:39Z"–"2026-08-27T14:09:07Z". The conclusion (event date = 2026-08-25) is right and is now better supported than the record claims, but the stated basis is factually wrong — and the dateModified of 2026-08-27 is exactly the live-document signal the BRIEF requires be recorded.

refuted.fact: unverified_or_excluded: 「Newsroom 的 Atom feed 只有 20 筆、最舊到 2026 年 9 月，回溯不到 8 月」(used to justify excluding the M5 Pro / M5 Max debut date)
refuted.why: REFUTED. I fetched https://www.apple.com/newsroom/rss-feed.rss (200, 18,825 B): 20 entries, newest 2026-09-16, oldest 2026-08-11T13:59:21.581Z. The feed reaches well into August and in fact carries all three 2026-08-25 releases. The exclusion of the M5 Pro/M5 Max debut date is still correct (the window does not reach back far enough), but the stated reason is false and must be rewritten.

refuted.fact: sourcing_notes: Apple Newsroom archive 列表頁「curl 只拿到篩選器介面、零筆文章列」
refuted.why: REFUTED. https://www.apple.com/newsroom/archive/ returns 200 / 322,881 B and contains 10 distinct article links (/newsroom/2026/09/…: iPhone 18 Pro, AirPods 5, iPhone Duo, Siri AI, Apple Watch Series 12, child safety, Emmy, etc.). It is not zero rows — it renders the current month server-side. The practical conclusion (cannot page back to August without JS) still holds.

refuted.fact: not_said: 「三篇稿都沒有出現 TSMC、台積電、foundry 等任何字眼」
refuted.why: REFUTED as literally written: "Foundry" appears twice in the Mac Studio release ("Up to 15.4x faster CopyCat ML training performance in Foundry Nuke…") — that is Foundry, the VFX software vendor, not a semiconductor foundry. TSMC / 台積電 / 代工 are genuinely absent from all six pages (I checked each term individually), so the editorial rule (do not add a foundry) stands, but the sentence must be narrowed or a reader/checker will think it is wrong.

refuted.fact: unverified_or_excluded: 4.5x vs 4.3x 的差異「Apple 未說明兩者量測口徑差異」
refuted.why: PARTLY REFUTED. Apple does disclose differing conditions: the chip release footnote 3 states testing in AUGUST 2026 with preproduction Mac Studio M5 Ultra 36c/80c/256GB vs Mac Studio M3 Ultra 32c/80c/256GB vs M1 Ultra 20c/64c/64GB; the Mac Studio release footnote 1 states testing in JULY 2026. Different months, and where configs are given they differ (256GB vs the 512GB/8TB baseline in the Studio release's footnote 2). The two figures should be presented with those disclosed differences, not as an unexplained contradiction.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[43]: 「…註腳說明對照基準是『前一代 Mac Studio 搭載 M3 Ultra（32 核心 CPU、80 核心 GPU、512GB 統一記憶體、8TB SSD）』，測試由 Apple 於 2026 年 7 月進行」as the basis for all four headline numbers (4.3x AI / 2x storage / 1.8x graphics / 1.3x CPU)
unsupported.why: The page's own <sup> markers say otherwise. Body: "up to 4.3x faster AI performance,<sup>1</sup> up to 2x faster storage,<sup>2</sup> up to 1.8x faster graphics,<sup>1</sup> and up to 1.3x faster CPU speed,<sup>1</sup>". Footnote 1 = "Testing was conducted by Apple in July 2026. See apple.com/mac-studio for more information." ONLY. Footnote 2 = "Results are compared to previous-generation Mac Studio systems with Apple M3 Ultra, 32-core CPU, 80-core GPU, 512GB of unified memory, and 8TB SSD." So that configuration backs the 2x STORAGE claim alone; Apple does not state a comparison configuration for the 4.3x AI, 1.8x graphics or 1.3x CPU figures in this release. Rewrite or the article will attribute a condition Apple never attached.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[32]: 「Mac mini 稿：AI 4 倍／儲存與圖形 2 倍／CPU 40%…註腳說明比較基準是 M4（10 核心 CPU、10 核心 GPU、32GB、2TB SSD），測試於 2026 年 7 月」
unsupported.why: Same conflation, mirrored — and note the Mac mini release numbers its footnotes in the OPPOSITE order to the Mac Studio release. Mac mini fn1 = the M4 baseline config; fn2 = "Testing was conducted by Apple in July 2026." Body: "up to 4x faster AI performance,<sup>1</sup> 2x faster storage<sup>2</sup> and graphics,<sup>1</sup> and 40 percent faster CPU performance.<sup>1</sup>" So the 2x storage figure carries only the date footnote, with no stated baseline. Anyone reusing the record's phrasing across both releases will get the footnote numbers backwards.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[31]: 「支援 16 種語言（含繁體中文）」
unsupported.why: The number 16 does not appear anywhere in the source. Footnote 4 enumerates names: English, Danish, Dutch, French, German, Italian, Norwegian, Portuguese, Spanish, Swedish, Turkish, Vietnamese, Chinese (simplified), Chinese (traditional), Japanese, Korean. The count is the researcher's arithmetic. It happens to be 16, but the BRIEF requires every number to trace to source text — state the list or say 「官方列出的語言中包含繁體中文」 instead of asserting a figure Apple never printed.

Not a verbatim string. The page renders "PRESS RELEASE" and "August 25, 2026" as two separate elements; the " / " is the researcher's. The underlying substance (press release label + 2026-08-25 date, repeated in the "Text of this article" block) is confirmed, but a field labelled verbatim_quote must be copied, not composed.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[38]: verbatim_quote "Up to 8.5x faster LLM prompt processing in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro"
unsupported.why: The page reads "Up to 8.5x faster LLM prompt processing performance<sup>5</sup> in LM Studio when compared to Mac mini with M2 Pro, and up to 4x faster than M4 Pro.<sup>2</sup>" — the word "performance" is dropped. The figures are right; the quote is a retype, not a copy. Systematic issue: several English quotes (facts 6, 8, 12, 15, 16, 17, 25) also replace Apple's em dash "—" with a plain hyphen "-", which the BRIEF explicitly warns against.

unsupported.fact: not_said: 「Apple 沒有列出『全球最快的 CPU 核心／單執行緒效能』是和哪些競品、哪些基準測試比的。註腳只寫 shipping competitive systems and select industry-standard benchmarks」
unsupported.why: Two different footnotes are merged. <sup>1</sup> ("Testing was conducted by Apple in August 2026 using shipping competitive systems and select industry-standard benchmarks") is attached to the LEDE sentence ending "…world's fastest CPU core … up to 170GB/s of unified memory bandwidth." The body sentence "It delivers the world's fastest single-threaded performance and up to 1.2x faster multithreaded performance as compared to M5, and up to 2.4x faster than M1." carries <sup>2</sup>, which names only Apple's own three Macs and no competitor at all. The conclusion (Apple never names a competitor or benchmark) is correct; the footnote attribution is not.

unsupported.fact: verified_facts[42] and [55]: recycled-content percentages (Mac mini 50%, Mac Studio 35%, 40% renewable energy) recorded with is_vendor_claim=false
unsupported.why: These are Apple's own measurements, each carrying a methodology footnote ("Product recycled or renewable content is the mass of certified recycled material relative to the overall mass of the device…"). Under the BRIEF (廠商宣稱的能力、評測數字一律寫成「Apple 說明」) they must be attributed, not written as neutral fact. Flag them as vendor claims before drafting.

additional_findings: MATERIAL OMISSION — overlaps_existing_article is wrong in substance. It says 「站上目前沒有任何 tech-news-* 內容包…沒有既有科技文章可重複」 after checking only ai-news-* and tech-news-*. But apps/api/app/guides/content/local-ai-on-mac-mini.json (zh-TW title 「Mac mini 當家用 AI 伺服器：統一記憶體、售價與區網設定」, sources checked_on 2026-09-14) already contains M6 (12 mentions), M5 Pro (9), NT$29,900 (2), NT$59,900 (2), 170GB (4) and 307GB (4) — i.e. exactly the unified-memory ladder and NT$ prices the editorial_brief proposes as this article's centrepiece table. local-llm-hardware-requirements.json and apple-intelligence-guide.json also overlap. The BRIEF's 「不要重寫既有文章講過的事」 rule applies and the overlap section must be redone before drafting.

The two 4.x figures do not just differ numerically — Apple labels them differently. Chip release: "up to 4.5x the peak GPU compute for AI compared to M3 Ultra" / TW「AI 的 GPU 峰值運算能力最高可達 M3 Ultra 的 4.5 倍」. Mac Studio release: "up to 4.3x the peak AI compute performance of M3 Ultra" / TW「AI 峰值運算效能最快可達 M3 Ultra 的 4.3 倍」. GPU-only peak compute vs whole-system AI compute performance. The record frames it purely as inconsistent numbers; the differing metric wording is the more defensible thing to write.

MISSING FIGURE — the Mac Studio release gives an M5 Max headline AI number the record never captured: "M5 Max features phenomenal on-device AI compute with up to 3.9x faster AI performance than the prior generation" / TW「M5 Max 具備出色的裝置端 AI 運算能力，AI 效能最快可達前一代的 3.9 倍」. fact 44 records M5 Max cores, 40-core GPU, 50% GPU and 614GB/s but not this.

MISSING ASYMMETRY — Mac mini: 「Mac mini 在供應鏈製造過程中所使用的電力，均來自風能與太陽能等再生能源」(100%, plus offsets for customer use); Mac Studio: 「供應鏈使用 40% 可再生能源」. The record captured only the Studio's 40%. If either number is used, the asymmetry must be stated or the 40% will read as Apple's ceiling.

MISSING FRAMING — the Mac Studio release says the 80-core GPU "brings Neural Accelerators to the Ultra chip for the first time", which is a cleaner first-party 'what is new' line than the record's spec-only phrasing, and belongs alongside the quad-die 'a first for Apple silicon' framing.

FOOTNOTE NUMBERING DIFFERS BY LOCALE AND BY RELEASE — the record notes the TW Mac Studio environment footnotes are 4/5 vs US 5/6, but the same shift also applies to the TW Mac mini (recycled/packaging are 5/6 in TW vs 6/7 in US) because the TW pages carry no Siri AI footnote. I confirmed Siri AI count: us-mini 12, us-studio 12, tw-mini 0, tw-studio 0, both chip pages 0.

CONFIRMED AND SOLID (the bulk of the record): every chip spec I checked matches the page with identical numbers and units — M6 2 nm, 12-core CPU = 2 super + 4 performance + 6 efficiency, 12-core GPU with a Neural Accelerator per core, Dual 16-core Neural Engine, 32GB / 170GB/s (+10% vs M5, 2.5x vs M1), ~30% peak GPU compute for AI vs M5 and >8x vs M1, 50% geometry rates, 1.2x MT vs M5 / 2.4x vs M1; M5 Ultra quad-die via UltraFusion from two dual-die M5 Max, >4.4TB/s inter-die, >6x connection density, up-to-36-core CPU = 12 super + 24 performance, 1.25x ST / 1.3x MT vs M3 Ultra, up-to-80-core GPU, 40% graphics vs M3 Ultra, 32-core Neural Engine, 512GB / 1.2TB/s (+50% vs M3 Ultra), 'hundreds of billions of parameters'; M5 Pro 18c/20c/64GB/307GB/s; M5 Max 18c (6 super + 12 performance)/40c/128GB/614GB/s; all NT$ prices (29,900/26,590; 59,900/56,390; 84,900/78,090; 199,900/185,390), the TW 8/27 09:00 pre-order, 9/22 availability and 512GB late-October; US $899/$799, $1,699/$1,599, $2,499/$2,299, $5,499/$5,099, pre-order 'today, August 25' in 30 countries and regions including the U.S. All verified word-for-word against the pages I fetched.

The chip release genuinely contains no price, no pre-order date and no availability date (I confirmed zero occurrences of 'pre-order', 'starts at', 'September 22', '(U.S.)'), so the record's headline correction to the candidate list — that 「官方未說明售價與上市日期」 is true of the chip release only, not of the event — is correct. Apple also never lists which 30 countries and regions (TW pages do not mention the 30 at all), never names a foundry, never gives transistor counts, die area, clocks, TDP or absolute TOPS, and never cites Geekbench/Cinebench/3DMark (0 hits in all three US releases). Those exclusions all hold up.
